model.title: CLEAR LABELS Act
model.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee · Sen. Rick Scott (R-FL)

summary.text: The bill would require drugs and the active ingredients used to make them, when sold in the U.S., to carry labels naming the companies that made them and where those companies are located. A finished packaged drug would need to list the original maker of each active ingredient, the original maker of the finished product, and any packer or distributor, either printed on the label or available electronically. Active ingredients would need similar labeling showing their original manufacturers. The Food and Drug Administration would decide whether violations count as misbranding and could assess civil fines, weighing factors such as whether the violator was first notified and given a chance to fix the problem. The agency would also coordinate with U.S. Customs and Border Protection on overlap with rules for imported drugs. These requirements would take effect five years after enactment.
